corrections.text: The article says Phoronix reported that 'Canonical had commissioned a security audit of Rust Coreutils that identified 113 issues in total, most since addressed'. Phoronix is relaying a Canonical blog post by Ravi Kant Sharma and says the full audit report by Zellic had not been made public, so the 113 total and the 'addressed' status are Canonical's figures. Phoronix's own CVE counts disagree (44 CVEs in its opening paragraph; 70 CVEs plus 73 other issues in the body), and the uutils 0.9.0 notes say the findings were 'widely reported as 44 CVEs'; the article uses only the 113 total, which both Phoronix passages give.

The article says The Register 'reported the same bug' as Phoronix. The Register describes a new bug in how Rust cp interprets the -L switch and says the team has reverted to GNU cp for now; it does not mention image builds or a Launchpad report. That this is the bug Phoronix described on 3 July 2026 is an inference from the matching cp -L behaviour and the dates, not something the Register states.

The article says the two sudo-rs fixes were 'sent to 25.10 users as a stable release update'. Phoronix wrote on 11 November 2025 that Ubuntu 25.10 'is also seeing a stable release update (SRU)' and that the package 'is being SRU'ed to users'; none of the cited sources confirms that the update had reached users.
